PullRequest.Title: Fix compact application menu spacing
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334615

## Summary

Keep activity-rail spacing out of nested compact application menus. The floating-rail margin selector also matched menu rows and separators, increasing normal 24px row steps to 32px at default density and 28px at compact density.

- Scope the gap selector to non-menu action bars and their own direct action items.
- Preserve the activity rail spacing and overflow calculations while restoring standard menu-row and separator spacing.
- Add real-widget regressions for default density, compact density, compact activity-bar size, and classic layout.
- Add keyboard-driven component fixtures for both densities in dark, light, and dark high contrast.

## Validation

- **44 targeted tests passed** across Modern UI, activity-bar sizing, Menu, and MenuBar:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/activitybar/activitybarPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/menu/menu.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/menu/menubar.test.ts \
  --grep "ActivitybarPart|^Menu|activity bar|floating rail|compact application menu"
```

- The default/compact density regressions failed against the original selector. All four new regressions passed with the fix, including a repeat after baseline screenshot capture.
- All six themed fixture variants retain 24px menu-row steps with no added rail margin, while preserving the default/compact rail gaps of 8px/4px.
- Verified keyboard navigation: Undo to Redo, skipping the separator to Cut, Left/Right submenu navigation, and Escape returning focus to the application-menu button.
- ESLint, stylelint, editor diagnostics, diff checks, and pre-commit hygiene passed.

## Manual verification

In the web workbench with Modern UI and the compact application menu in the activity bar, open Edit. Check normal row and separator spacing at default and compact density, then verify keyboard entry and dismissal. Repeat in light and high-contrast themes.

Menu placement and overflow reports #334616 and #334886 remain separate.

## Screenshots

Captured from the same real-widget component fixture at default density, with Edit selected and Undo focused. The fix restores menu spacing without changing the rail gap.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and keyboard-navigate the compact application menu while Modern UI floating panels are enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing MenuBar key handler reads the compact button geometry, appends the Menu DOM, and the browser performs style/layout before painting. The changed CSS participates in that existing style resolution but adds no JavaScript work or boundary call.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of adjacent ActionBar items beneath activity-bar content, typically a bounded set of rail icons; nested application-menu and submenu rows are removed from the effective match cardinality by the change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser main-thread event and render pipeline; menu construction and style/layout are sequential, with no worker, queue, limiter, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. A cold first open may require normal stylesheet matching and layout; subsequent opens may reuse browser style data, but MenuBar already reconstructs the menu on each open and this diff does not change that lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed production hunk is a single selector whose child combinators constrain matching to direct ActionBar items outside a direct .monaco-menu parent; MenuBar's existing open path contains only DOM/style/layout work and no network, filesystem, IPC, database, or subprocess operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact selector-matching time depends on DOM size and browser style-cache state, but the changed selector is more restrictive than the prior descendant selector and does not increase matched menu rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Before the diff, the broad descendant selector also matched nested menu rows and separators; after the diff, matching is restricted to the rail's own direct action items, reducing affected elements without introducing additional layout reads or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lay out or restyle the floating activity rail when density or compact activity-bar mode changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ActivitybarPart synchronously updates bounded CSS custom properties and classes, followed by the browser's normal style/layout pass. The selector consumes the existing gap variable to space adjacent rail actions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Adjacent direct activity-rail actions; cost grows linearly with the bounded number of rail items, while nested menu items no longer contribute.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single main-thread style update and render pass; no parallel work or burst of asynchronous operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit cache or invalidation mechanism changed. Browser style caching may make repeated restyles warm, while class/custom-property changes invalidate the same rail subtree as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ActivitybarPart publishes the existing gap property during compact-style updates, and the changed CSS only narrows which descendants receive the margin.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of installed activity icons varies by user, but it remains a small UI collection and the selector's effective match set is narrower than before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves existing rail spacing and overflow assumptions while excluding nested menus; it does not add repeated computation, forced layout, allocation, or an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the new compact-menu browser regressions and themed component screenshot fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test-only code constructs ActionBar/MenuBar widgets, waits one animation frame in four unit-test variants, then performs synchronous geometry/style reads; screenshot fixtures render two density variants across three themes. This work is outside product startup and interaction paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed four density/layout unit-test cases plus two fixtures expanded to three themes each; menu row counts are fixed in the fixture definitions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each individual test/fixture performs its DOM setup and geometry reads serially on the browser main thread; runner-level parallelism is not established by the changed code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixtures create fresh widget state per variant and dispose it afterward; there is no changed cache, persistent key set, or warm-cache dependency. Markdown image URLs are documentation references and are not fetched by application execution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all added TypeScript outside the CSS hunk is under test/component-fixture paths, with fixed loops and explicit disposal; inspected menu paths contain no fetch/XHR, IPC, filesystem, database, or subprocess call on normal rendering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CI runner scheduling and screenshot-capture overhead are external to these hunks, but the added cardinality is fixed at four unit-test cases and six themed fixture variants rather than user-input-scaled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression. The added synchronous layout measurements are bounded regression-test work, and the fixture additions do not alter shipped runtime behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. The sole production change narrows a CSS selector, reducing nested menu matches; added layout reads and widget construction are fixed-cardinality test-only coverage. No actionable performance finding or qualifying shipped regression fix was established.
